neighbours.label: a relative pronoun (who, that, which) after a noun someone wants, seeks or needs (a king who would..., a remedy that would...); relatives on a specific, known noun stay quiet
fire: The village was hoping for a doctor who would stay through the winter.
She spent years looking for a teacher who could explain the proofs.
The firm badly needs a manager who understands small suppliers.
Reformers demanded a constitution that would protect the poor.
Engineers set out to design a bridge that could survive earthquakes.
My parents wanted a house which had room for all of us.
The coach is seeking a striker who can finish under pressure.
The union called for a law that would ban night shifts.
quiet: The doctor who stayed through the winter has moved to Leeds.
Over the years I met the teacher who explained the proofs.
Yesterday the firm fired the manager who hired those suppliers.
Historians admire the constitution that protected the poor.
Tourists like to photograph the bridge that survived the earthquake.
We sold the house which my parents built for all of us.
Fans cheered the striker who scored under pressure.
The union praised the law that banned night shifts.

short: relative after a wanted or sought-for noun
